hypotheses.justification: The statement is still true without this hypothesis; it only picks out the degenerate case, which can be handled directly. By definition (line 175), `planeExponentDifference r s = fun i => (s i : ℤ) - (r i : ℤ)`. Proof without the hypothesis: split on whether some `s ∈ f.support` satisfies `s ≠ r`. If one does, run the existing proof unchanged; it only uses this hypothesis to obtain such an `s`. If none does, every `s ∈ f.support` equals `r`, so `planeExponentDifference r s = planeExponentDifference r r = 0`. Take `v := fun _ => 1`, which is nonzero, and `k := 0`; then `0 • v = 0` holds (by `funext` and `simp [planeExponentDifference]`). An empty support is a special case of this branch and holds trivially. The other two hypotheses are needed. Without `hr`: take `f` with support `{s, t}` and `r` off the line through `s` and `t`. Any determinant built from two support points has a repeated vector and is zero, so the rank-two condition fails, but `s - r` and `t - r` are not parallel. Without `hnrank`: take three non-collinear support points.
